entries.issuing_body: New York County Supreme Court (as reported)
entries.title: New York court denies the Attorney General's temporary restraining order motion against Kalshi, with a report-back on 2026-11-30 and a preliminary injunction hearing in early January 2027
entries.facts: Three news outlets report that on Monday 2026-11-23 a New York state court denied the New York Attorney General's motion for a temporary restraining order against Kalshi. Sportsbetting Dime names the judge as New York Supreme Court Judge Melissa A. Crane and quotes her as saying that she is not seeing the factors she needs to issue an injunction on this very preliminary basis. Front Office Sports identifies the court as New York County Supreme Court, states that the moving party was the office of the New York Attorney General, and states that the denial does not mean she has ruled on the merits. All three outlets report that counsel for both sides were asked to confer on potential safeguards concerning access by people aged 18 to 20 and to report back on Monday 2026-11-30, and that a hearing on New York's request for a preliminary injunction is expected in early January 2027, with Front Office Sports reporting that an in-person hearing will be scheduled for either January 7 or January 8. The ruling was made from the bench. No signed order was available to retrieve, the New York Attorney General's press-release listing carries no statement dated 2026-11-23, and no court index number is reported by any of the three outlets.
entries.source_label: Sportsbetting Dime report of the 2026-11-23 bench ruling, corroborated by Front Office Sports and Cointelegraph. No court order or docket entry was retrieved, because the ruling was delivered from the bench.
entries.relevant_to: prediction-market platforms, sports-event-contract venues, licensed sportsbooks, state-licensed gaming operators

entries.title: Coinbase Derivatives sets security futures customer margin at no less than 15.05 percent, and states an intention to accept payment stablecoins as margin only if federal regulators first amend their margin rules or grant relief
entries.facts: The SEC published a notice of filing and immediate effectiveness of a proposed rule change by Coinbase Derivatives, LLC, a designated contract market registered with the CFTC, as Release No. 34-106923, File No. SR-COIN-2026-003, in the Federal Register of 2026-11-20 at 91 FR 75421 to 75424. The filing was made concurrently with the CFTC. The notice states that the exchange is submitting the proposed rule change to establish customer-level margin requirements for security futures, and that Rule 1215(b) provides that the margin requirement for a long or short position shall not be less than 15.05 percent, which the notice describes as higher than the 15 percent federal minimum. Under Rule 1215(c), acceptable assets are limited to deposits of cash, margin securities subject to specified restrictions, exempted securities, any other assets permitted under Regulation T of the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System, any other assets permitted under CFTC Regulation 41.46 and SEC Rule 242.404, and any combination of the foregoing. Payment stablecoins are not among the assets currently listed as acceptable. In a paragraph headed Type, Form and Use of Margin, at 91 FR 75422, the notice states a conditional intention: if the SEC, the CFTC or the Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System amend SEC Rule 242.404, CFTC Regulation 41.46 or Regulation T respectively, or otherwise provide exemptive or interpretive relief, then the exchange intends to permit Participant Firms and Clearing Firms to collect payment stablecoins as margin. Comments are due on or before 2026-12-11.
entries.source_label: SEC notice, Federal Register of 2026-11-20, document 2026-23653, retrieved in full from the govinfo Federal Register PDF
entries.relevant_to: designated contract markets, futures commission merchants, security futures intermediaries, stablecoin issuers, crypto derivatives venues

entries.title: SEC charges Backward Hat Capital and its co-founders over a 560 million dollar offering fraud in which investor funds were promised to be converted to crypto assets for FX arbitrage
entries.facts: In press release 2026-116 of 2026-11-20, titled SEC Charges Indianapolis-Based Backward Hat Capital and Its Co-Founders With $560 Million Dollar Offering Fraud and Obtains Emergency Relief, the SEC states that the defendants fraudulently raised approximately $560 million from more than 2,000 investors. The release states that Williams and Johnson promised that investor funds would be converted to crypto assets and then used to engage in FX arbitrage. The SEC states that the action was filed in the U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Indiana and that it has obtained emergency relief. The release refers to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, which brought its own action in the same matter on 2026-11-17. The release states no civil action number.
entries.source_label: SEC press release 2026-116 of 2026-11-20, retrieved in full from sec.gov
entries.relevant_to: fund managers, retail forex intermediaries, crypto asset platforms, investor-facing fintech distributors

entries.title: NYDFS issues a cybersecurity alert to all entities it regulates on active threat campaigns using the ARTEX agentic AI framework
entries.facts: The New York State Department of Financial Services published an industry letter dated 2026-11-21, titled Cybersecurity Alert: Active Threat Campaigns Using ARTEX Agentic AI Framework, addressed to organizations and individuals regulated by the Department. The letter states that the Department encourages regulated entities to take proactive steps to reduce their cybersecurity risk exposure, and sets out four steps covering securing internet-facing platforms, strengthening detection and monitoring, prioritizing vulnerability remediation, and preparing for rapid containment. The letter is framed as encouragement and states no deadline. Its addressees include every category of NYDFS-regulated entity. The body of the letter does not use the terms virtual currency, BitLicense, cryptocurrency, digital asset, money transmitter or payment.
entries.source_label: NYDFS industry letter of 2026-11-21, retrieved in full from dfs.ny.gov
entries.relevant_to: New York licensed financial institutions, virtual currency licensees, limited purpose trust companies, money transmitters
